On 25 September 2018, around 20 gunmen riding camels attacked three commercial vehicles on the road south of Gereida (South Darfur). The perpetrators fled south after being chased by relatives and those living in the IDP camp, and the victims were taken to hospital.

It is likely these events are a continuation of a clash from the previous week (which has been vaguely attributed by the source to a dispute relating to membership forms for the NCP party).

On 8 September 2018, 12 armed herders attacked a police vehicle in the Nue area of Tawila locality (coordinates for Tawila, North Darfur, used). Police and an unspecified security force (coded here as the Sudanese military) gave chase, killing two herders, wounding three, and arresting two The police were guarding farmers in the area.

Police fired tear gas (wounding one person, who was hit by a cannister), whilst demonstrators and police clashed. Demonstrators also blocked roads, though through unspecified means.

On 8 April 2021, hundreds of women marched in Khartoum (Khartoum state), calling for the abolition of discriminatory laws; greater progress at combating political exclusion and ensuring safety of women and girls; for Sudanese authorities to sign international charters on equal rights for women; and for special courts to be established to handle cases of gender-based violence. During the demonstration, a vehicle intentionally ran over a protester (who survived, but was injured), before its occupant 'physically and verbally assaulted' protesters, before being apprehended by police.

On 8 April 2021, hundreds of protesters gathered at the main UN offices in Khartoum (Khartoum state), calling for protection for civilians and the displaced in West Darfur, and for the removal of RSF paramilitaries from the state, following series violence in El Geniena in recent days.

On 8 April 2021, Resistance Committees representing workers from the central bus terminal in Khartoum (Khartoum state) began a sit-in protest at the station, calling for the removal of several officials who have been accused of corruption. Police dispersed the demonstrators, and arrested four.
On 10 April 2021, a group of people gathered in Khartoum (Khartoum, Khartoum) in demonstration against poor living conditions and continuous interruption of electricity and water.

On 11 April 2021, a group of people gathered in Khartoum (Karthoum, Khartoum) to demonstrate against poor living conditions and continuous interruption of electricity and water. Rioters blocked main roads and set fire to tires. Police dispersed them with tear gas. There were demonstrations also in Ondurman, Nyala and El Fasher.

On 25 February 2021, a small gathering of Ethiopian supporters of the Benishangul Peoples Liberation Movement took place at the British Embassy in Khartoum (Khartoum state). The demonstration was in opposition to the Ethiopian government and its actions in Benishangul-Gumuz region, and appeared to have been agitating for a transfer of territory from Ethiopia to Sudan.

On 18 April 2021, demonstrators began a sit-in protest at a hospital in Khartoum (Khartoum state), denouncing the failure of hospital authorities to adequately preserve dead bodies in the morgue, some of whom are likely among those reported missing in the June 3rd massacre. Demonstrators called for the dismissal of the Director of Forensic Medicine, and for justice for the victims of the massacre.

On 25 April 2021, hospital guards (coded as Private Security) and police attempted to disperse a sit-demonstration in Khartoum (Khartoum state) which related to the failure of hospital authorities to adequately preserve dead bodies in a hospital morgue. 2 were seriously injured (through unspecified means) as a result of the intervention. One source indicates an unspecified Islamist group was involved in planning the dispersal, but does not elaborate on details.

Around 1 April 2021 (week of), workers from the Civil Aviation Authority demonstrated in the front of the offices of the Authority in Khartoum (Khartoum state), calling for the removal of the director of the Authority (for reasons which are unspecified in the source).

Other: On 29 April 2021, Minni Minawi Arko - who leads one of the two main factions of the SLM/A rebellion (and was the only one of these factions to sign the Juba Peace Agreement) - was appointed Governor of Darfur. The precise powers of the Governor have not been defined, nor have the existing five states of Darfur been merged into a single administrative system. The development is likely to raise tensions in parts of Darfur, and further strain protracted peace talks with Minawi's rival Abdul Wahid el Nur, who commands the more militarily significant faction of the SLM/A based in Jebel Marra. Event coded to Khartoum (Khartoum state).

Around 3 May 2021 (as reported), former workers at the Presidential Palace in Khartoum (Khartoum state) demonstrated at their former place of employment, demanding to be reinstated and to receive financial compensation for their dismissal.

Around 3 May 2021 (as reported), police dispersed a sit-in protest at the Civil Aviation Authority in Khartoum (Khartoum state), firing tear gas at the workers who had been demonstrating for a month in front of the offices of the Authority. The workers were calling for the dismissal of the director of the institution.

On 4 May 2021, citizens from the Kalma area of Darfur (including IDPs) marched in Khartoum (Khartoum state), denouncing attacks against Kalma IDP camp and alleged plans to close the camp; for the governor to be dismissed and disarmament of the area; and for justice for those killed, injured and detained as a result of the violence.

On 5 May 2021, staff at the Khartoum Teaching Hospital (Khartoum state) and Resistance Committee members began a sit-in demonstration at the hospital, calling for the dismissal of the hospital director after four staff members critical of the director were removed from their positions.

On 10 May 2021, relatives of army officers who were executed by the Bashir regime in 1990 gathered in Khartoum (Khartoum state), demanding justice, and calling for the location of their grave site to be disclosed.

On 11 May 2021, thousands of demonstrators (including Resistance Committee members) blocked roads with burning tires and rocks at several location in Khartoum (Khartoum state), and marched to the site of the June 3rd/Ramadan massacre at the army HQ. SAF personnel opened fire using live rounds, tear gas, and stun grenades, with some demonstrators throwing rocks at the soldiers. 2 demonstrators were killed and 37 wounded; authorities claim to have arrested the soldiers who fired upon the demonstrators. Demonstrators subsequently gathered at the Royal Care Hospital in southern Khartoum, where one of the victims later died, and began a sit-in demonstration which lasted until late May.

Around 24 May 2021 (as reported), unknown armed men wearing civilian clothes fired upon the Resistance Committee-organized sit-in protest at 60th Street in Khartoum (Khartoum state), wounding several. The sit-in protest has been in operation since 11 May, and has called for justice for those killed by security forces during and after the uprising.

On 3 April 2021, a Resistance Committee activist was taken from a sit-in demonstration at the hospital in Khartoum (Khartoum state) by an unknown group, with his body returned to the hospital the following day. The victim had been beaten to death.

On 3 June 2021, thousands of demonstrators (including Resistance Committee members) marched in Khartoum (Khartoum state), demanding justice for those killed during the 3 June massacre of 2019, and for a correction in the course of the revolution. Some demonstrators called for the dissolution of the partnership between civilian and military branches of the transitional government. Police fired tear gas against the demonstrators, a small number of whom threw stones and molotov cocktails at the police. A policeman was also shot and killed during the demonstration by an unknown person.

On 6 June 2021, an unidentified man stabbed and killed a 16 year-old Resistance Committee member who was a participant of the ongoing sit-in demonstration at the hospital in Khartoum (Khartoum state). The suspect has since been arrested.
On 6 June 2021, former government bank workers who had been dismissed under the Bashir regime demonstrated in Khartoum (Khartoum state), calling for their reinstatement.
On 9 June 2021, children suffering from cancer and their parents demonstrated against shortages of essential medication at the Ministry of Health in Khartoum (Khartoum state).

On 10 June 2021, residents of Al-Ma'ali demonstrated at the Electricity Distribution Company offices in Khartoum (Khartoum state), condemning the lengthy delays to a project which was supposed to introduce electricity and electric lights to the neighborhood, which began seven or eight years ago.

On 10 June 2021, thousands of demonstrators (including Resistance Committee members) gathered in Greater Khartoum (events coded in Khartoum, Khartoum North (Bahri locality), and Omdurman, all in Khartoum state) to attend SPA-organized demonstrations to denounce the removal of fuel subsidies, which is anticipated to cause a doubling of fuel prices. Some demonstrators called for the replacement of the current transitional government. Roads were barricaded with rocks and burning tires, whilst reports of robberies at barricades by gangs were reported. Reports have suggested that supporters of the dissolved National Congress Party have been present at the demonstrations, though this is currently unconfirmed.

On 11 June 2021, SPA-organized demonstrations (attended by Resistance Committee members) continued in Khartoum (Khartoum state), denouncing the decision to end fuel subsidies. There is limited information on the second day of demonstrations.

Around 11 June 2021 (as reported), Sudanese expatriates who had recently returned to Sudan demonstrated in Khartoum (Khartoum state), after the Minister of Trade issued an edict preventing the importation of cars into the country (which would affect the vehicles they had been intending to bring back to the country with them).

On 14 June 2021, dozens of people in Khartoum (Khartoum, Khartoum) gathered in demonstration against the contribution of an Italian company called Salini Impregilo in the construction of the Renaissance Dam. The group gathered in front of the Embassy of Rome.

On 15 June 2021, a group of auditors from the General's Court in Khartoum (Khartoum, Khartoum) gathered in demonstration to demand the dismissal of national authorities and improvement of their work conditions. Auditors clashed with each other.
On 12 June 2021, demonstrators gathered once more in Khartoum (Khartoum state) as part of SPA-organized demonstrations against the removal of fuel subsidies.

On 20 June 2021, dozens of children undergoing treatment for cancer demonstrated at the Ministry of Health in Khartoum (Khartoum state), denouncing the lack of essential supplies needed to maintain their treatment.

On 22 June 2021, Resistance Committees demonstrated in Khartoum (Khartoum state), demanding the release of 13 activists who had been arrested on 15 June in connection with the death of a police officer, stating that they activists had been wrongfully arrested.

On 24 June 2021, employees of the Savings and Social Development Bank demonstrated in Khartoum (Khartoum state), after accounts linked to several employees of the bank were frozen as a result of an anti-corruption investigation.

On 27 June 2021, police arrested at least 79 individuals linked to the former ruling NCP regime in Taif and other areas of Khartoum (Khartoum state), and seized an unspecified quantity of weapons and explosives, along with maps showing the Ministry of Defence building. Among the arrested was a former Major General from NISS; a pro-NCP journalist; and members of the Popular Security Forces.

On 30 June 2021, about 250 supporters of the disbanded NCP demonstrated against the Transitional Government in Khartoum (Khartoum state), calling for its overthrowal. 200 NCP supporters were arrested by police, who also fired tear gas at the crowds.

On 30 June 2021, thousands of demonstrators (including Resistance Committee and Communist Party supporters, and members of the Arab Baath party) gathered in the Greater Khartoum area (three events coded to Khartoum, Khartoum North, and Omdurman, all in Khartoum state), calling for justice for those killed in the course of the uprising and denouncing the Transitional Government for failing to honor the goals of the revolution, amid economic turmoil and austerity measures (including the removal of fuel subsidies). Some demonstrators called for the RSF to be integrated into SAF. Demonstrators burned tires in the street, and clashed with police, who fired tear gas and rubber bullets, wounding at least 2 demonstrators (one source says 28; a leading member of the Communist Party was also wounded in the hand). Authorities stated that 52 police officers were injured in the demonstrations (one seriously), around half of whom were wounded in Khartoum North and the remainder in central Khartoum. 73 were arrested. Note that in Khartoum, five Beja were wounded and 'dozens' arrested during the demonstrations, according to the Beja Supreme Council.

On 4 July 2021, four unidentified gunmen attacked the Christian Affairs Minister advisor in square next to Al-Salameh grocery area south of Khartoum (Khartoum State). He was beaten with the back of the gun and insulted with profanity and threatened with liquidation if he did not stop opening church files with the Disempowerment Committee and the Ministry of Religious Affairs.
Around 6 July 2021 (as reported), university lecturers protested in Khartoum (Khartoum state), calling for improvements to pay and for pay scales to be standardized.

On 9 July 2021, local residents marched and demanded the recovery of the lands of the Hamadab are of Khartoum (Khartoum state). The demonstrators began a sit-in protest which has lasted at least four days.

Around 13 July 2021 (as reported), a number of expatriates demonstrated at the Ministry of Finance, denouncing the customs tariff for importing cars in in Khartoum (Khartoum state). This follows several similar demonstrations in recent months.

On 13 July 2021, local street vendors protests against the authorities who launched campaigns against them to prevent them from practicing their activity along Jackson's street in Khartoum (Khartoum state). At least 17 people were arrested by police.

On 14 July 2021, employees of the Ministry of Culture protested demanding the dismissal of the Minister of Culture in Khartoum (Khartoum state), amid what they describe as an abrupt deterioration of the Ministry.

On 15 July 2021, lawyers and the families of victims of the Ramadan massacre protested in front of the Public Prosecution office in Khartoum (Khartoum state). They demanded the resignation of the public prosecutor, after he was accused of preventing forensic investigators from Argentina from assisting Sudanese investigations into the killings.
On 21 July 2021, local residents carried a demonstration during the Eid al-Adha celebration and demanded the recovery of the lands of the Hamadab area of Khartoum (Khartoum state).

On 21 July 2021, former employees of the Civil Aviation Authority who were dismissed from their jobs demonstrated in Khartoum (Khartoum state). The demonstrators demanded salaries dating back to January 2021, and to also receive their Eid grant.
On 28 August 2021, members from the regular armed forces attack a journalist in Khartoum (Khartoum state). The Sudanese Journalists Network condemned the act by forces and called for press freedom.

On 31 August 2021, member from Agricultural Bank Retirees Association organized a sit in demonstration in front of the Council of Ministers calling for the implementation of Cabinet Resolution in Khartoum (Kahrtoum). They demanded their pensions and other benefits to approved.

On 31 August 2021, students demonstrated against the dismissal of the dean of student affairs at the Al-Neelain University in Khartoum (Kahrtoum). The students accused the administration and unnamed parties of being behind his dismissal.

On 27 July 2021, the people of Sortony area organized a peaceful march in front of the Ministry of Justice building in Khartoum (Khartoum state) to present a memorandum to the Minister following the recent violations in the Sortony IDP camp. They demanded accountability for those responsible for the killing and displacement of IDPs at the camp.

On 2 August 2021, real estate owners organized a demonstration in front of the Ministry of Justice demanding an amendment to the law in Khartoum (Khartoum state). The owners was affected by the Building Lease Act of 1991.

On 2 August 2021, residents of Northern state organized a demonstration in Khartoum (Khartoum state), following serious road accidents in their home state. Demonstrators demanded improved road maintenance, and greater efforts by authorities to regulate speed and driving standards.

On 2 August 2021, a committee of parents of students studying abroad carried out a demonstration in front of the Council of Ministers officers in Khartoum (Khartoum state), demanding a solution to the problem of students studying abroad, following the new procedures for adjusting the exchange rate.

On 2 August 2021, students of the University of Khartoum began a sit-in demonstration in Khartoum (Khartoum state), denouncing the failure of university authorities to address student welfare and housing needs.

On 4 August 2021, lawyers as well as family members of victims of the Ramadan massacre demonstrated in Khartoum (Khartoum state), demanding the removal of the Attorney General and Public Prosecutor, amid concerns about lengthy delays in the investigation into the massacre.

On 1 August 2021, expatriates who had their vehicles seized by customs authorities organized a sit-in demonstrations in front of the Council of Ministers in Khartoum (Khartoum state), stating the seizure of their vehicles was unfair.
Around 9 August 2021 (as reported), kidney patients staged a sit-in demonstration in Khartoum (Khartoum state). This is after dialysis operations were halted.

On 9 August 2021, supporters of Lt. Col. Ali Rizkallah who arrested alongside other members of Musa Hilal's Revolutionary Awakening Council following clashes in 2017, organized a demonstration in front of the Republican Palace in Khartoum (Khartoum state), demanding his release.

actor1: Military Forces of Sudan (2019-) Military Intelligence Service
notes: On 23 August 2021, members of the Military Intelligence service assaulted a journalist and another person, who were seriously injured, near the army headquarters in Khartoum (Khartoum state).

On 24 August 2021, dozens of journalists demonstrated in front of the Press and Publications Council in solidarity with a journalist who was attacked by the military intelligence service in Khartoum (Khartoum state). They demanded justice and freedom of speech.

On 24 August 2021, hundreds of medical students at Al-Neelain University in Khartoum (Khartoum state), held a sit in demonstration outside the college building, demanding the dismissal of the dean of the Faculty of Medicine.

On 26 August 2021, local resident demonstrated in front of the council of ministers office over the high price of essential goods in Khartoum (Khartoum state). Police officers fired teargas canisters to disperse the group.

On 6 September 2021, students of Al-Neelain University staged sit-in demonstration in front of the Ministry of Higher Education buildings (Khartoum state), denouncing the dismissal of an academic at the University, and calling for the resignation of the Director of the University.

On 6 September 2021, radio and television workers organized a demonstration sit-in in front of the cabinet buildings in Khartoum town (Khartoum state), demanding good working conditions, health allowances and increase of working allowance by 75%.
On 9 September 2021, employees of the Nile Bank demonstrated in Khartoum (Khartoum state) in solidarity with the victims of a deadly robbery in Nyala.

On 13 September 2021, Resistance Committee members organized a sit-in demonstration in front of the Public Prosecution office in Khartoum (Khartoum state), demanding the release of two activists who were arrested for chanting slogans against the Deputy Head of the Sovereign Council.

Around 13 September 2021 (as reported), medical students from East Kordofan University (one source says West Kordofan University) demonstrated at the Ministry of Higher Education (event is assumed to have taken place at the national-level ministry in Khartoum rather than the state-level ministry, though the source is ambiguous with regards to its description of locations), denouncing the severely compromised nature of their education, and calling for the government to send them to an alternative universities in the country. Note that one source suggests the protest has been ongoing since 3 September, though this is unclear.
On 19 September 2021, a lieutenant in the police assaulted and confiscated items from a journalists at the Democrat newspaper in Khartoum (Khartoum state).

Coup/military takeover: On 21 September 2021, the military announced that it had foiled a coup attempt in Khartoum (Khartoum state), with Military Intelligence likely involved in thwarting the coup. The specific identity of the coup plotters is not established beyond the fact that some elements of the army were involved (with speculation suggesting that former NCP members, Islamist officers, and/or unspecified civilian politicians were involved). Doubts have been expressed regarding the authenticity of the coup, with a number of commentators suggesting that the coup attempt was masterminded by senior officers in the army for unknown political ends.
On 21 September 2021, citizens demonstrated in Khartoum (Khartoum state), condemning the failed coup attempt. The demonstrators were calling for civilian rule.

On 24 September 2021, residents of Manaser in River Nile state organized a sit-in demonstration in Khartoum (Khartoum state), demanding roads, electricity, health and education for the people in the locality. The demonstration followed demonstrations in Manaser earlier the week.

On 26 September 2021, an unspecified women's group from both civil society and political organizations staged a sit-in protest in front of the cabinet building in Khartoum (Khartoum state) condemning the failed coup attempt, and accusing the security services of failing to provide security in the country.

On 26 September 2021, thousands of citizens gathered inside the headquarters of the Empowerment Removal Committee in Khartoum (Khartoum state), condemning the withdrawal of military forces guarding the committee headquarters, which were withdrawn amid escalating tensions between civilian and military factions within the Transitional Government.

On 27 September 2021, members of the police assaulted two women and a male lawyer in El Deim neighborhood in Khartoum (Khartoum state). One of the women sustained injuries on the face and the lawyer was beaten on the head, face, and ears. The reason for the attacks is unclear.

actor1: FFC: Forces for Freedom and Change
notes: Change to armed group: Around 27 September 2021 (as reported), a number of rebel groups who had signed the Juba Peace Agreement announced that they were establishing a new faction of the FFC, following attempts at reunifying the disparate components of the alliance by PM Hamdock earlier in the month. The most prominent members of this (as yet unnamed) faction are JEM and SLM/A (Mini Minnawi faction), with several figures and minor rebel factions (including Al-Amin Daoud; a small faction of the SPLM-North under Khamis Jalab; and the Tamazuj and Third Front groups) also splitting from the FFC [event coded to Khartoum].

On 27 September 2021, members of Resistance Committees (who appear to include Resistance Committee members from Omdurman as well as South Kordofan state) as well as bank employees and SPA representatives of the Kenana Sugar Factory, organized a protest vigil at the headquarters of the Empowerment Removal Committee in Khartoum (Khartoum state) calling for the civilianization of Sudanese politics.

actor1: Police Forces of Sudan (2019-) General Intelligence Service
notes: On 28 September 2021, General Intelligence Service raided Islamic State hideouts in the Jabra and El Azhari neighborhoods of southern Khartoum (Khartoum state). Five GIS personnel were killed in the operation, and one wounded . Eleven foreign nationalities were arrested in the operation, with the remaining four members who escaped during the operation arrested the following day.

On 28 September 2021, medical students from East Kordofan University demonstrated at the Ministry of Higher Education in Khartoum (Khartoum state), demanding the government to send them to alternative universities. The demonstration follows a sit-in protest by the students, who have drawn attention to serious inadequacies in the provision of education at the University.

On 29 September 2021, four Islamic State militants killed a driver in Khartoum (Khartoum state) while attempting to evade capture from security forces. It is not clear whether the driver was part of the Islamic State cell. The four militants were captured.
On 29 September 2021, doctors demonstrated in Khartoum (Khartoum state), demanding the return of equipment needed to treat cancer patients which had recently been transferred from Khartoum Hospital.

On 29 September 2021, members of the Communist Party protested in Khartoum (Khartoum state), demanding the end to military involvement in the Transitional Government; calling for the provision of essential services and the rebuilding of infrastructure; and denouncing the World Bank.

On 30 September 2021, about 20,000 people demonstrated in Khartoum (Khartoum state), calling for civilian rule. Many protesters came from outside Khartoum by train from the cities of Atbara and Madani, as well as from Sennar and White Nile states. The police forces fired teargas canisters to disperse the crowd, and one demonstrator sustained a head injury.

On 3 October 2021, activists who had been injured during the uprising of December 2018 started a sit-in protest in front of the Council of Ministers in Khartoum (Khartoum state). The demonstrators accused the government of failing to fulfil pledges to provide treatment and housing for the wounded.

On 5 October 2021, health officers gathered in front of the office of the Director-General of the Ministry of Health in Khartoum (Khartoum state), demanding improvements to environmental standards, and for unspecified management problems to be resolved.

On 6 October 2021, the family of a lady who died due to a medical error involving excessive use of an anaesthetic gathered in front of the Medical Council in Khartoum (Khartoum state), calling for accountability for those responsible for her death.

On 7 October 2021, dozens of students from the University of Khartoum barricaded University Street in Khartoum (Khartoum state) using unspecified means to do so, in a demonstration against the deteriorating conditions of the university, and the lack of electricity and water services. Police had earlier used tear gas to disperse the group when they began a sit-in protest at the University itself.

On 3 October 2021, students of the University of Khartoum organized a sit-in protest demanding the dismissal of the university director in Khartoum (Khartoum state), after an attack by a criminal group on a female boarding house.

On 4 October 2021, dozens of doctors and citizens staged a protest in front of the Northern Police Station in Khartoum (Khartoum state), demanding the release of a medical doctor arrested after being part of a demonstration in September at the Jackson Square area.

On 12 October 2021, students of the University of Medical Sciences and Technology demonstrated in Khartoum (Khartoum state), demanding the release of the chairman of the university's board of trustees, and describing his dismissal as being motivated by politics.

On 14 October 2021, activists from Eastern Sudan organized a sit-in protest in front of the Cabinet headquarters in Khartoum (Khartoum state), demanding be brought to justice for those involved Kassala event and calling for justice for those who died in the course of the uprising.

On 14 October 2021, a number of expatriates organized a protest in front of the Ministry of Finance in Khartoum (Khartoum state), calling for cars which had been confiscated in a long-running customs dispute to be released.

On 14 October 2021, hundreds of lawyers organized a protest vigil near the Republican Palace in Khartoum (Khartoum state), demanding civilian rule and amendment of the constitution. The regular forces (coded as SAF) prevented the group from reaching the palace. A Major General beat and insulted a journalist covering the protest.

On 16 October 2021, three thousand five hundred demonstrators from the breakaway FFC National Accord faction gathered in front of the presidential palace in Khartoum (Khartoum state), calling for the military to dissolve the transitional government and take power. Demonstrators also removed security barriers around government buildings and prevented the police and security forces from going about their work. The sit-in has so far continued for six days.

On 19 October 2021, members of the SLM/A-Minnawi Faction assaulted journalists (including AFP photographers and the crew of Al Jazeera) during their coverage of the ongoing sit-in protest at the palace in Khartoum (Khartoum state). Some photographers were harassed and beaten.

On 21 October 2021, hundreds of thousands of demonstrators gathered for nationwide demonstrations in Khartoum (Khartoum, Khartoum state), calling for continued civilian rule and democratic transition. Security forces (assumed military forces) assaulted journalists including a BBC correspondent and prevented them from filming in the presidential palace sit-in protest in Khartoum. Some photographers were harassed and beaten.

On 24 October 2021, hundreds of demonstrators supporting the military blocked (through unspecified means) the Mak Nimr Bridge and Nile Street in Khartoum (Khartoum state), calling for the government to dissolve. Police fired teargas canisters to disperse the group.

On 25 October 2021, tens of thousands of demonstrators gathered in Khartoum (Khartoum state), Bahri locality, and Omdurman denouncing the military coup. Security forces fired teargas canisters and live bullets to disperse the crowd. At least 7 people were killed, including a South Sudanese student. Fatalities were distributed across three events. Two people died in Khartoum on 28 Oct and 15 Nov from injuries sustained during the event on this day.

Coup/military takeover: On 25 October 2021, military forces dissolved the civilian government, arrested the prime minister and some members of the cabinet in Khartoum (Khartoum state). The military declared state of emergency in the country.

actor1: Military Forces of Sudan (2019-2023) Rapid Support Forces
notes: On 26 October 2021, members of RSF attacked female university students at dormitories in Khartoum (Khartoum state). No further details reported.

On 27 October 2021, security forces along with the Sudan Liberation Movement (Minawi Faction) fired live bullets at demonstrators at the Sixtieth Street in Khartoum (Khartoum state) who were denouncing the military coup. Some of the demonstrators were injured.

On 30 October 2021, tens of thousands of demonstrators responded to the call by the Resistance Committee for nationwide demonstrations in Khartoum (Khartoum state) denouncing the military coup. The security forces fired teargas canisters and live bullets to disperse the crowd. Unspecified number of demonstrators were injured. One person died in Khartoum on 5 Nov following the injuries the victim incurred during the event on this day.

On 6 November 2021, Resistance Committees closed most of the main roads using barricades (unspecified means) in Khartoum (Khartoum state), denouncing the military coup. The security forces fired teargas canisters and bullets to disperse and remove the barricades.

On 7 November 2021, teacher committees demonstrated in front of the headquarters of the Ministry of Education in Khartoum (Khartoum state), denouncing the military coup and the appointment of employees of the former regime in Ministry of Education. The committee also reported that 87 teachers have been detained so far. Security forces fired teargas canisters to disperse the crowd and assaulted some of the teachers, injuring them.

On 7 November 2021, Resistance Committees continued to closed most of the main roads using barricades (unspecified means) in Khartoum (Khartoum state), denouncing the military coup. The security forces fired teargas canisters and bullets to disperse and remove the barricades.

actor1: Military Forces of Sudan (2019-2023) Rapid Support Forces
notes: On 9 November 2021, the RSF paramilitaries deployed at the Africa street in Khartoum (Khartoum state) attacked a civilian, beating him, and forcibly shaving his head for having a 'Western' hairstyle.
On 11 November 2021, staff of Petro energy and DAL food companies organized protest vigils in front of their offices in Khartoum ( Khartoum state), denouncing the military coup.

On 11 November 2021, demonstrations were held in the neighborhoods of Khartoum (Khartoum state), denouncing the formation of new Transitional Sovereignty Council (TSC) by the military and calling for a civilian led government.

Around 10 November 2021 (week of), police arrested four men, including a South Sudanese national, in Hai Mayo and took them to the Yarmouk police station in Khartoum (Khartoum state), where they were tortured. The South Sudanese national succumbed from his injuries while the three others sustained severe injuries.

On 12 November 2021, local residents and South Sudanese nationals from Hai Mayo area, stormed Yarmouk police station in Khartoum (Khartoum state), damaging some properties, including vehicles and motorcycles, after a South Sudanese national who was arrested, died in police custody.

On 16 November 2021, the Journalists Network members demonstrated near the British Council in Khartoum (Khartoum state), condemning the arrest of the director of Al-Jazeera's office, a journalist at Darfur 24 website, and the continued harassment of journalists covering demonstrations denouncing the coup.

On 21 November 2021, military leaders who seized power through a coup on October 25 signed a political agreement with the former prime minister [event coded to Khartoum, Khartoum state]. The agreement reinstated the PM to lead a transitional government and the Sovereignty Council, and has led to the replacement of several cabinet ministers with 'technocrats'. The agreement has been rejected by several prominent members of the FFC.

On 2 December 2021, citizens from Jebel Mun organized a protest vigil in front of the UNITAMS mission in Khartoum (Khartoum state), condemning the violence between pastoralists and farmers, and demanding intervention in the border area with Chad. They called for the dissolution of the Sudanese-Chadian joint forces and the closure of the border with Chad.

On 8 December 2021, Sudanese journalists and activists organized a sit-in protest in front of the Kuwaiti building in Khartoum (Khartoum state) in solidarity with Hala 96 Radio, which has been closed after the military coup. The group demanded the reopening of the media house closed due to repressive decisions and measures, and compensation for all the losses.

On 8 December 2021, residents from the West and North Darfur states protested in front of the United Nations mission and the Council of ministers headquarters in Khartoum (Khartoum), denouncing the attacks in Jebel Moon, Al Kereinik, and Zamzam IDP camp.

On 9 December 2021, people living with disabilities organized a demonstration in Khartoum (Khartoum state), denouncing the military coup and rejecting the political agreement between the reinstated prime minister and military leaders.

On 9 December 2021, demonstrators, organized by the Resistance Committee, gathered in the El Doyoum El Shargiy area in Khartoum (Khartoum state) to denounce the attacks on villages in West and North Darfur.
